# gitmoap_repository_mirror (Data Source)

Get a repository's mirror. What the repository follows, how often, when it last synced and how that went, and whether the source has moved since. Anyone who can see the repository may read it.

The token needs `import:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_mirror" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository ID

### Read-Only

- `interval_minutes` (Number) How often it syncs, in minutes.
- `last_sync_at` (String) When it last synced.
- `last_sync_error` (String) Why the last sync failed.
- `last_sync_result` (String) How the last sync went: `ok`, or `failed`.
- `next_sync_at` (String) When it next syncs.
- `paused_reason` (String) Why it is paused, when it is: `setter_lost_access` (the person who set it can no longer push
here, or closed their account) or `moved_organization` (the repository moved to another
organization, which the token was not sealed for). Either lasts until somebody who can push
sets the mirror again.
- `repository_id` (String)
- `run_pipelines` (Boolean) Whether a sync starts its pipelines.
- `set_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--set_by))
- `source_ahead` (Boolean) Whether the source has moved since the last sync, when that was checked.
- `source_url` (String) What it follows.

<a id="nestedatt--set_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `set_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor, and empty on a redacted one and on an outside author.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor and on an outside author (`imported`).
- `imported` (Attributes) An author who wrote on another host — a work item, a merge request, a comment, a release an import
brought — and whom nobody here is linked to yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--set_by--imported))
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--set_by--imported"></a>
### Nested Schema for `set_by.imported`

Read-Only:

- `identity_id` (String) The outside author's id among the organization's imported identities.
- `login` (String) Their login on that host.
- `name` (String) Their name on that host, when it gave one.
- `profile_url` (String) Their profile's address on that host, when it gave one.
- `source_host` (String) The host they wrote on, such as `github.com`.
